population.span: 302 hospitalized patients receiving antibiotics were randomized to receive Lactobacillus GG, 20 x 10(9) CFU/d, or placebo for 14 days.

endpoint.span: The primary outcome was the proportion of patients who developed diarrhea in the first 21 days after enrollment.

estimate.span: Diarrhea developed in 39 (29.3%) of 133 patients randomized to receive Lactobacillus GG and in 40 (29.9%) of 134 patients randomized to receive placebo (P=.93).

analysis_set.span: Results were analyzed in an intention-to-treat fashion.

treatment_strategy.span: 302 hospitalized patients receiving antibiotics were randomized to receive Lactobacillus GG, 20 x 10(9) CFU/d, or placebo for 14 days.

follow_up.span: The primary outcome was the proportion of patients who developed diarrhea in the first 21 days after enrollment.

absent_reason.ci: Neither held abstract reports a confidence interval; P=.93 is a P value, not a confidence interval.

entry_population_matches_question.why: The randomized entry population comprised hospitalized patients receiving antibiotics, within the question's population.
